body:
Windows subtitle users can now move, lock, pass through, configure, and close the floating bilingual caption from its own hover toolbar. The caption remains a fixed transparent subtitle surface; the Echo main window keeps only enable and emergency recovery controls.

The change adds separate WinUI toolbar and settings HWNDs alongside the existing layered Direct2D caption HWND. Settings preview live and persist through the existing preferences; position lock and click-through stay independent, and the main-window recovery action disables pass-through and unlocks the overlay.

Validation: Windows Release x64 build completed with 0 warnings and 0 errors; all 193 CoreChecks passed. An isolated MSIX GUI run with synthetic bilingual text exercised settings persistence, click-through and lower-window hit testing, drag/lock, emergency recovery, main-window minimization, and three close/reopen cycles. A separate hover test confirmed the toolbar hides after the pointer leaves. Later UI Automation reruns showed stale-element and drag-coordinate instability; those diagnostics are recorded in the source evidence folder. This machine has one display, so second-monitor and live DPI changes remain unverified.

No macOS files or recording/recognition flows were changed. This PR targets the open Windows UI parity branch and is not merged.
title: feat(windows): add floating subtitle controls and settings
